statement.p: Suppose that z is a linear function of x and y with slope 3 in the x direction and slope 5 in the y direction.
(a) A change of 0.2 in x and -0.3 in y produces what change in z?
(b) If z=7 when x=8 and y=7, what is the value of z when x=7.8 and y=6.7?

static.solution:
(a) Since z is a linear function of x and y with slope 3 in the x direction, and slope 5 in the y direction, we have: z = 3 x + 5 y + c. We can write an equation for changes in z in terms of changes in x and y: \Delta z = (3 (x + \Delta x) + 5(y + \Delta y) + c) - (3 x + 5 y + c) = 3 \Delta x + 5 \Delta y. Since \Delta x = 0.2 and \Delta y = -0.3, we have \Delta z = 3 (0.2) + 5(-0.3) = -0.9. So a 0.2 change in x and a -0.3 change in y produces a -0.9 change in z.
(b) As we know that z=7 when x=8 and y=7, the value of z when x=7.8 and y=6.7 will be z = 7 + \Delta z = 7 + 3\Delta x + 5\Delta y. where \Delta z is the change in z when x changes from 8 to 7.8 and y changes from 7 to 6.7. We have \Delta x = 7.8 - 8 = -0.2 and \Delta y = 6.7 - 7 = -0.3. Therefore, when x=7.8 and y=6.7, we have z = 7 + 3 \cdot(-0.2) + 5\cdot(-0.3) = 4.9.
